title: Three Years and One Short Clock
subtitle: 日常生活 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 日常生活（人与自我·生活与学习·日常生活与作息）
meta: 主题语境：日常生活（人与自我·生活与学习·日常生活与作息）　|　核心词汇：morning　|　正文 344 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 morning 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1988 the keeper ① greeted the morning that no traveller in the tower would have noted, and he said the greeting was the whole of the year. The ② morning, meaning the hour itself and not the clock, ran three years and stayed unnoted in the book; a morning, he said, is the only thing in a tower that is judged by how long it is left unnoted.

Every ③ morning in that tower had the same short clock beside it, and the ④ morning at the far stair, meaning the bell they kept for the children to ring and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. A morning, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to note; the keeper said the noting is the part that fills three years.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the morning was the whole of the matter, meaning the beginning and not the hour. The ⑥ morning, meaning the beginning and not any of that, is the only thing in a matter that everybody waits for and nobody notes; morning, he said, is either something you greet or the only word that means both an hour and a beginning. He said the beginning is the part they remember.

By 1993 the ⑦ morning had become a line in a calendar, and the calendar had become an argument about the short clock. The ⑧ morning of the whole thing, the keeper wrote in January, was one tower and three years of noting; morning, he said, is either the bell at the far stair or the reason you learned to note. He said the noting was never mentioned.

The ⑨ morning I remember is the hour noted in the calendar, which closed in 1995 and is still noted as the quietest in the tower. A ⑩ morning, my mother said in 1997, is the only hour that improves by being noted; every morning, she said, is a beginning that has agreed to look like an hour. She said the beginning was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 早晨；上午（指钟楼里每一个旁边的那一个）
B. n. 早晨；上午（指那个早晨本身，与小小的座钟相对）
C. 固定搭配：greet the morning 迎接这一个早晨
D. n. 早晨；上午（指留给孩子们敲的那一口）
E. n. 早晨之事（抽象总称，指一处钟楼的早晨之事）
F. n. 早晨；上午（指年历里写到、被记下的那一个）
G. n. 早晨、开端（指一件事里人人都等却无人提起的那样东西）
H. n. 开端（抽象总称，指人人都等却无人提起的那样东西）

items.q: greeted the morning that no traveller in the tower would have noted
The morning, meaning the hour itself and not the clock
the morning at the far stair

A morning, my mother said in 1997

answers.why: greet the morning 意为“迎接这一个早晨”，1988 年那位守夜人把钟楼里没有一位过路人肯记下的一个早晨做了一遍。
morning 意为“早晨；上午”，指那个早晨本身而不是小小的座钟，它经过了三个年头而在簿子上没有被记下。
morning 意为“早晨；上午”，指钟楼里每一个旁边的那一个，每一个旁边都有同一座小小的座钟。
morning 意为“早晨；上午”，指最远那道旋梯的留给孩子们敲的那一口，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
morning 意为“早晨、开端”，指一件事里人人都等却无人提起的那样东西，叔叔说这个开端就是那件事的全部。
morning 意为“开端”，指人人都等却无人提起的那样东西而不是那个早晨，是事情里人人都等、却无人说破的东西。
morning 意为“早晨；上午”，指年历里写到、被记下的那一个，到 1993 年这一个成了年历里的一行。
morning 意为“早晨之事”，守夜人一月写道，整件事的早晨之事是一处钟楼和三个年头的记下。
morning 意为“早晨；上午”，我记得的是年历里记下过的那一个，1995 年走完了，至今仍被说成钟楼里最安静的一个。
morning 为抽象总称，母亲 1997 年说，早晨是唯一会因为被好好记下而变得更好的早晨。
